title: Knowledge check: The Express.js Security Model

questions.prompt: In The Express.js Security Model, which statement best describes Security responsibilities of Express and the application?
options: Trace the request from client through middleware and route/service logic to its response. Keep HTTP concerns separate from business rules and data access.
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Protect the boundary in layers: validate input, apply the control appropriate to the risk, test unauthorized and malformed requests, and review dependencies and deployment configuration.
questions.answer_key: Protect the boundary in layers: validate input, apply the control appropriate to the risk, test unauthorized and malformed requests, and review dependencies and deployment configuration.
questions.explanation: Protect the boundary in layers: validate input, apply the control appropriate to the risk, test unauthorized and malformed requests, and review dependencies and deployment configuration.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying The Express.js Security Model?
options: Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

Use secure configuration, HTTPS, narrow origin allowlists, secure cookies, rate and payload limits, parameterized database access, dependency updates, and context-aware output handling. One control never replaces authorization.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
questions.answer_key: Use secure configuration, HTTPS, narrow origin allowlists, secure cookies, rate and payload limits, parameterized database access, dependency updates, and context-aware output handling. One control never replaces authorization.
questions.explanation: Use secure configuration, HTTPS, narrow origin allowlists, secure cookies, rate and payload limits, parameterized database access, dependency updates, and context-aware output handling. One control never replaces authorization.

questions.prompt: A change related to The Express.js Security Model appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
